page: Amazon Web Services x8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the system provides 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs clocked at 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache along with advanced instructions including AVX-512 and AMX. The hardware configuration features 3,072 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 7 GHz, providing a resource allocation of 16 GB of RAM per core. The server does not bundle local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, directing external data traffic over a 75 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark evaluations show exceptional parallel processing capacity and memory throughput. The server attains top-tier results in multi-core metrics, registering 209,138.43 in stress-ng multi-core testing and 22,085.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Data transfer measurements record uncached read throughput of 525.98 GB/sec and small-block cached read throughput exceeding 15.4 TB/sec. The architecture also excels in high-volume transaction testing, sustaining 271.51 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier PassMark database processing metrics, while single-core compute performance remains in the middle to upper tiers.

From an architectural standpoint, consolidating 3 TB of DDR5 memory within a dedicated bare-metal chassis delivers high compute density for memory-bound tasks. This structure eliminates hypervisor virtualization penalties and minimizes intra-node latency compared to distributed multi-node clusters. A key architectural tradeoff is the complete reliance on network-attached storage over the 75 Gbps interface, making network I/O configuration a critical factor for disk-persistent operations.

Amazon Web Services x8i.metal-48xl is specifically built for enterprise-scale in-memory databases, extensive Redis or Memcached distributed caches, high-throughput ETL data pipelines, and large CPU-driven inference tasks.
